input: Register my business name with the state formally

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Registering a trade name (DBA) is a very different process from forming an LLC or corporation — the steps, forms, and costs differ significantly.
Each U.S. state (or country) has its own filing authority, fees, and requirements — the entire process depends on which jurisdiction applies.
Whether this is a solo venture, a partnership, or involves co-owners affects which registration type is required and who must sign filings.
The user may have a hard deadline — such as a contract start date or a launch date — which determines whether expedited filing is needed.
Some users want to DIY the filing; others want to hire a registered agent or attorney — this shapes what the action plan looks like.
The user may just want the name protected, or they may also need an EIN, bank account, or licenses — knowing the end goal scopes the full checklist.
Whether the business will operate only locally or across multiple states affects whether state-level registration alone is sufficient or federal trademark filing is also needed.

gold.taskTitle: Register Business Name Formally With the State
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to officially register their business name with their state government, but key details about the business structure, location, timeline, and goals are needed to build the right plan.

questions.title: What type of business entity are you registering?
questions.description: Is this a sole proprietor DBA (doing business as), an LLC, a corporation, or another structure? The registration process differs entirely by entity type.

questions.title: Which state will you be registering the business in?
questions.description: The filing authority, required forms, fees, and processing times are specific to each state. Knowing the state is essential to map out the correct steps.

questions.title: Will this business have co-owners or partners?
questions.description: A multi-owner business may require a partnership agreement, multiple signatories on filings, or a specific entity type like an MMLLC or general partnership.

questions.title: Do you have a deadline by which this must be registered?
questions.description: A hard launch date, contract requirement, or funding milestone may mean standard processing times are too slow and expedited filing needs to be factored in.

questions.title: Do you plan to file yourself or hire a professional?
questions.description: DIY filing via the state portal is cheaper but requires more guidance; using a registered agent service or attorney changes what the action steps look like.

questions.title: What does fully done look like beyond the name registration?
questions.description: Some users only need the name on file; others also need an EIN, a business bank account, operating licenses, or a seller's permit — clarifying this scopes the full plan.

questions.title: Will the business operate in multiple states or just one?
questions.description: Operating across state lines may require foreign qualification filings in other states or a federal trademark, going beyond a single state registration.
